quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Don't let the spelling of "thin" guide you — isolate the exact consonant sound and test it against both options.
quests.explanation: "thin" targets /θ/. Made by placing your tongue tip lightly behind your top teeth and blowing with no voice, it's a voiceless dental fricative — distinct from the voiceless alveolar fricative /s/, which instead calls for pushing a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with no voice.
quests.mouthPosition: Place your tongue tip lightly behind your top teeth and blow with no voice.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: For /f/, the trick is to rest your top teeth lightly on your bottom lip and blow with no voice — like the start of "fan". Check whether "fast" really does that.
quests.explanation: What makes "fast" contain /f/ rather than /v/ comes down to articulation: /f/ means you rest your top teeth lightly on your bottom lip and blow with no voice, while /v/ would instead mean resting your top teeth lightly on your bottom lip and blowing with your voice on.
quests.mouthPosition: To produce this sound, rest your top teeth lightly on your bottom lip and blow with no voice.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: "bath" needs careful listening. A voiced bilabial plosive like /b/ can sound close to a voiceless bilabial plosive like /p/ if you're not paying attention to exactly what your mouth is doing.
quests.explanation: Once you isolate the consonant in "bath", it's clearly /b/ — produced by pressing both lips together and releasing with your voice on. Words with /p/ instead, like "pie", require pressing both lips together and releasing with no voice.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel it in the mouth: press both lips together and release with your voice on.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Whisper "race" to yourself and freeze on the target consonant. Is your mouth doing this — pushing a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with no voice — or this — pushing a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with your voice on?
quests.explanation: /s/ is the sound in "race", formed by pushing a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with no voice. Learners often mix this up with /z/, a voiced alveolar fricative made by pushing a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with your voice on, but the mouth is doing something different each time.
quests.mouthPosition: Push a thin stream of air over your tongue tip with no voice.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: The two candidates for "tag" feel different in the mouth: /t/ means you tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with no voice, and /θ/ means you place your tongue tip lightly behind your top teeth and blow with no voice. Which matches?
quests.explanation: This is /t/, not /θ/: in "tag", you tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with no voice. The distractor would instead need placing your tongue tip lightly behind your top teeth and blowing with no voice, which changes the sound completely.
quests.mouthPosition: To produce this sound, tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with no voice.
